units.truth: \mathcal M=\{y:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\mid y(x)=x^T\theta,\ \theta\in\mathbb R^d\}.
The task is to estimate theta; theta denotes the model parameters.
To include an intercept set x_1=1 for every object; then \theta_1 is the shift.
For a new object x, the prediction is \hat y(x)=x^T\hat\theta.
The squared loss is L(y,z)=(y-z)^2.
Least squares minimizes \sum_{i=1}^n L(y_i,\hat y(X_i))=\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-\hat y(X_i))^2=\|y-X\theta\|^2 over \theta\in\mathbb R^d.
y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)^T, X=(x_{ij})_{n\times d}, and \theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d)^T.
For f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R, \partial f/\partial x=(\partial f/\partial x_1,\ldots,\partial f/\partial x_d) is written as a row.
\nabla f is written as a column with entries \partial f/\partial x_1 through \partial f/\partial x_d.

units.truth: Maximum likelihood is introduced for iid X_1,\ldots,X_n with distribution P_\theta in a parameterized family indexed by \theta\in\mathbb R^d.
The family is assumed either continuous or discrete; p_\theta(x) denotes a density in the continuous case and P_\theta(X=x) in the discrete case.
L_X(\theta)=\prod_{i=1}^n p_\theta(X_i), treated as a function of \theta.
\hat\theta=\operatorname*{argmax}_{\theta} L_X(\theta).
For X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim N(a,\sigma^2), \theta=(a,\sigma) and p_\theta(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}\exp[-(x-a)^2/(2\sigma^2)].
L_X(\theta)=(2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}\exp[-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-a)^2].
\ell_X(\theta)=\log L_X(\theta)=-\frac n2\log(2\pi)-n\log\sigma-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-a)^2.
\frac{\partial\ell_X(\theta)}{\partial a}=\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-a)=0.
\hat a=\bar X=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n X_i.
\frac{\partial\ell_X(\theta)}{\partial\sigma}=-\frac n\sigma+\frac{1}{\sigma^3}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-a)^2=0.
\hat\sigma^2=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\bar X)^2=S^2.
The lower-left diagram contains three overlapping bell-shaped density curves, with peaks ordered left to right and a marked common x on the horizontal axis.
At the marked x, the diagram compares the heights of the different density curves; the curves have p_theta-index labels and the marked heights have L_x(theta-index) labels.
Consistency is expressed as \hat\theta\xrightarrow{P}\theta, equivalently P_\theta(\|\hat\theta-\theta\|>\varepsilon)\to0 as n\to\infty.

The third property at upper-right is blank at 5029 and 5039; at 5049 it is still being written. Its completion is excluded and must not be invented.

units.truth: The section title is Обучение и применение моделей.
\mathcal M=\{y:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal Y\} is the family of candidate models.
Обучение (оценка, вывод) is selecting a specific model \hat y\in\mathcal M from the training sample.
Метод обучения is the particular way of selecting \hat y\in\mathcal M.
The loss L(y,z) penalizes predicting z\in\mathcal Y instead of the correct answer y\in\mathcal Y.
\sum_{i=1}^n L(Y_i,y(X_i))\longrightarrow\min_{y\in\mathcal M}.
The apartment-price example has true price 10 million, predicted price 12 million, and squared penalty (10-12)^2=4.
